data.title: Nuvation Bio to broaden Phase III glioma trial into Europe
data.description:
Nuvation Bio is to expand its pivotal Phase III SIGMA trial into Europe to evaluate the investigational, oral, brain-penetrant, selective mutant isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1) inhibitor safusidenib in patients with IDH1-mutant glioma.

This trial will be expanded into six study sites in France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Sweden, and the UK.

The new sites build on existing trial activity in Australia, Canada, China, Japan, and the US, where recruitment is either underway or preparing to launch.

The randomised, placebo-controlled study is evaluating safusidenib as maintenance therapy for patients with high-risk IDH1-mutant astrocytoma who have undergone standard-of-care radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy alongside adjuvant temozolomide.

Progression-free survival, measured via blinded independent central review, serves as the primary endpoint. Around 300 participants are scheduled to take part in this main pivotal segment.

Alongside the core trial, an exploratory cohort plans to enrol nearly 40 chemotherapy- and radiotherapy-naïve participants with grade 3 IDH1-mutant oligodendroglioma to evaluate objective response rate.

Nuvation Bio founder, president and CEO David Hung said: “Our goal is to develop therapies that create a profound, positive impact on patients’ lives, and for safusidenib that means building a broad development programme that has the potential to reach more people with IDH1-mutant glioma in need of treatment options around the world.

“Expanding SIGMA to sites across six European countries is an important step for patients, and we have been encouraged by the strong interest in the study from physicians and the glioma community in Europe.

“We sincerely thank the investigators, site teams, patient advocates and patients who will help make this study possible.”

The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted fast track designation to safusidenib in August 2026 for IDH1-mutant glioma treatment.

Safusidenib is also undergoing assessment in the Phase III G307 study in territories where vorasidenib lacks approval or availability, as well as in the Phase II G209 trial for individuals whose cancer progressed following vorasidenib therapy.

In March 2024, Nuvation Bio dosed the first subject in a Phase I/II clinical trial of NUV-1511, a new drug-drug conjugate (DDC) aimed at treating advanced solid tumours.

data.title: First patient dosed in Nacuity’s Phase III Usher syndrome RP trial
data.description:
Nacuity Pharmaceuticals has dosed the first patient in its global confirmatory Phase III SLO-RP Preserve study, evaluating NPI-001 for retinitis pigmentosa (RP) associated with Usher syndrome.

The study will assess whether the oral treatment can reduce photoreceptor loss and slow the progression of the rare, progressive inherited retinal condition, which causes irreversible sight loss and lacks approved treatments to slow degeneration.

The double-masked, 24-month, randomised trial plans to recruit up to 80 adult patients.

They will receive either an NPI-001 or placebo tablet orally twice daily and attend nine clinical visits across a two-year timeframe.

Recruitment is under way in Australia and the US, with active sites including the Inherited Retinal Degeneration Clinic at the Retina Foundation of the Southwest in Dallas, Texas.

Nacuity chairman, CEO and co-founder Halden Conner said: “Dosing the first patient in our first Phase III trial marks a significant milestone for Nacuity and, more importantly, for the Usher syndrome community.

“We look forward to advancing NPI-001 through this confirmatory study as we work toward delivering a potential disease-modifying therapy for patients with RP associated with Usher syndrome.

“We’re grateful for our continued collaboration with the Retina Foundation of the Southwest and to the investigators, patients and families making this study possible.”

Formulated as an oral tablet manufactured to good manufacturing practice (GMP) standards, NPI-001 delivers N-acetylcysteine amide (NACA) to treat illnesses triggered by oxidative stress.

The therapy holds fast track, breakthrough therapy, and orphan drug designations from the US Food and Drug Administration for RP, the last of which grants seven years of regulatory exclusivity in the US following potential regulatory approval.

Beyond RP, Nacuity operates clinical programmes focusing on cataract and cystinosis.

data.title: Vanda reports Phase III tradipitant trial data in GLP-1-associated vomiting
data.description:
Vanda Pharmaceuticals has reported positive results from the Phase III clinical trial, Study 3601 (VP-VLY-686-3601), assessing its oral therapy Nereus (tradipitant) for the prevention of vomiting triggered by glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist treatments.

The placebo-controlled, randomised study showed marked reductions across overall, frequent, and severe vomiting episodes.

Following the trial, Vanda intends to review the combined findings from its Phase II and Phase III programmes with regulators and plans to submit a supplemental new drug application (sNDA) to the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to support tradipitant for this indication.

The trial tested the therapy, which operates as a neurokinin-1 receptor antagonist, under elevated emetogenic conditions by administering participants a single 1mg dose of semaglutide without standard clinical titration.

Across the trial population, 43.0% of patients receiving Nereus (61/142) reported vomiting compared with 58.5% on placebo (96/164), representing a site-adjusted relative reduction of 27%.

For the key secondary outcome measuring vomiting alongside severe nausea graded at 3 or above, incidence reached 33.1% in the tradipitant arm (47/142) against 50.6% in the placebo cohort (83/164), an adjusted 35% relative decrease.

Exploratory post-hoc assessments indicated substantial declines in higher-intensity vomiting patterns.

Frequent vomiting, defined as exceeding two events on more than one day, occurred in 6.3% of participants on tradipitant versus 15.9% on placebo, reflecting a 60% relative reduction.

Extreme vomiting of more than ten total episodes dropped by 81%, occurring in 2.8% of tradipitant recipients compared with 14.6% on placebo, consistent with an approximate 80% decrease recorded during Phase II testing.

Most vomiting occurred by day two, with incidence peaking on day one.

Vanda president, CEO and board chairman Dr Mihael Polymeropoulos said: “These results demonstrate that Nereus can meaningfully reduce vomiting and frequent multi-day vomiting induced by GLP-1 therapy, which are key contributors to treatment discontinuation.

“The consistency and magnitude of the effects observed across this programme could offer significant benefit to the millions of people seeking or using GLP-1 therapies.”

In May 2024, Vanda Pharmaceuticals reported positive outcomes from its second Phase III clinical trial of tradipitant, aimed at treating motion sickness.

data.title: Zhimeng Biopharma concludes enrolment in ALS trial of CB03-154
data.description:
Shanghai Zhimeng Biopharma has completed patient enrolment in the pivotal Phase II/III clinical trial of its investigational potassium-channel opener, CB03-154, for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

A total of 255 patients have been recruited across 15 clinical research centres in mainland China, and Professor Fan Dongsheng of the 3rd Affiliated Hospital of Peking University is the principal investigator.

The trial’s primary efficacy endpoint is the change from baseline in Revised Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Functional Rating Scale (ALSFRS-R) score at week 39.

Discovered and developed by Zhimeng Biopharma independently, CB03-154 showed neuroprotective effects on motor neurons through modulation of neuronal excitability, restoring the balance between excitation and inhibition, in preclinical studies.

Zhimeng Biopharma founder and CEO Dr Huanming Chen said: “I would like to extend my sincere appreciation to Professor Fan Dongsheng and the investigators at all clinical research centres across China for their dedicated efforts, as well as to all ALS patients and their families who participated in the trial for their selfless commitment.

“Moving forward, we will spare no effort to advance clinical development and regulatory submissions, striving to bring a truly effective new treatment option to ALS patients in China and around the world as soon as possible.”

The China Centre for Drug Evaluation (CDE) approved the initiation of the Phase II/III ALS trial in July 2025. The US Food and Drug Administration had previously granted CB03-154 orphan drug designation in October 2023.

If Phase II top-line data prove positive in the third quarter of 2027, the company intends to file a marketing application with the China CDE seeking conditional approval.

Zhimeng Biopharma said this approach is designed to give ALS patients earlier access to innovative treatments, reflecting its patient-centred development philosophy in rare diseases.

Beyond ALS, CB03-154 is advancing through clinical development in additional central nervous system (CNS) indications. As of October 2026, the drug had entered Phase II trials for focal epilepsy in both Australia and China.

data.title: Teva to halt Phase II MSA therapy trial after futility analysis
data.description:
Teva Pharmaceuticals has announced plans to halt a Phase II clinical trial evaluating emrusolmin (TEV-‘286) to treat adults with multiple system atrophy (MSA), after an interim analysis found the study was unlikely to meet its primary efficacy endpoint.

The decision followed a recommendation from the independent data monitoring committee (IDMC), which conducted a prespecified interim futility analysis of the TOPAS-MSA study.

IDMC’s review met the predefined futility criterion, suggesting a low probability of demonstrating efficacy if the trial continued.

Teva noted this was a predictive assessment rather than a final efficacy analysis. No safety concerns arose from the interim review.

An investigational, orally administered small molecule, emrusolmin targets alpha-synuclein aggregation, a core pathogenic mechanism expected to be involved in MSA, a rare neurodegenerative disorder. Teva is developing the therapy in collaboration with privately managed biotechnology company MODAG.

The randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled TOPAS-MSA trial is designed to enrol nearly 350 participants.

They were to receive either 300mg of emrusolmin or placebo for roughly 48 weeks, followed by a follow-up period of four weeks.

The primary endpoint measured change from baseline to week 48 in the modified Unified Multiple System Atrophy Rating Scale Part I score.

Teva global R&D executive vice-president and chief medical officer Eric Hughes said: “While we are disappointed by the outcome of this interim analysis for the Phase II study, we remain deeply committed to learning everything we can from these data.

“We are deeply grateful to the patients, families, investigators, and study teams who contributed their time and commitment to this research. Our hope is that the science and learnings can deepen our understanding of MSA and help us determine a path forward for emrusolmin.”

Teva said it would work with study investigators to ensure protocols are followed as the trial ends. The company also plans to share the findings with the scientific community after concluding a comprehensive analysis.

It said that the discontinuation applies only to the TOPAS-MSA study and does not represent a final decision on the emrusolmin programme as a whole.

Last month, Sanofi and Teva’s inflammatory bowel disease drug showed benefit in patients with both ulcerative colitis and Crohn’s disease.

data.title: Mondego Bio begins Phase Ia trial of oral MB‑388
data.description:
Mondego Bio has initiated a first-in-human Phase Ia clinical trial of MB‑388, an oral dual protein tyrosine phosphatase non-receptor type (PTPN2/PTPN1) inhibitor, which is designed to act in both tumour cells and immune cells to overcome resistance to cancer immunotherapy.

The placebo-controlled, randomised, double-blind trial is assessing MB‑388’s single and multiple ascending doses in healthy volunteers.

It aims to evaluate the therapy’s tolerability and safety, characterise its pharmacokinetics, and measure target engagement using blood-based pharmacodynamic biomarkers.

The company anticipates initial human pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic results in December 2026.

Mondego Bio subsequently plans to start a Phase Ib trial in January 2027 for patients with advanced solid tumours who progressed during or after standard treatment, including checkpoint inhibitors.

After monotherapy dose levels are cleared, the trial will incorporate a combination run-in with programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-(L)1) blockade covering both checkpoint-naive and checkpoint-refractory patients.

Readout from combination dose escalation is scheduled for December 2027.

Mondego Bio CEO Nikolay Savchuk said: “Starting the first clinical study of MB‑388 is an important milestone for Mondego. The Phase Ia study will define the relationship between exposure, pathway engagement and tolerability, giving us the data to move efficiently into our planned study in patients with cancer.”

In preclinical tumour models that responded or resisted PD-1 blockade, MB‑388 showed activity as a single agent and in combination with anti-PD-1 therapy, increasing intratumoral cluster of differentiation 8 (CD8)-positive T cells and granzyme B.

When tested against osunprotafib, a clinical-stage PTPN2/PTPN1 inhibitor, MB‑388 demonstrated higher oral exposure, longer target coverage, and a substantially higher unbound fraction in human plasma.

Based in Portugal, Mondego Bio focuses on developing small-molecule therapies that restore interferon-gamma signalling, increase antigen presentation, and enhance natural killer and T-cell function.

The company was founded with support from Biovance Capital, OrbiMed, and Torrey Pines Investment, with co-investment from the Fundo de Capital e Quase Capital, which is managed by Banco Português de Fomento and supported by the InvestEU Fund.

data.title: Tango and Erasca’s Phase I/II trial of ERAS-0015 combo opens for enrolment
data.description:
Tango Therapeutics and Erasca have begun enrolment for a Phase I/II trial assessing the combination of oral therapies ERAS-0015 and vopimetostat in patients with lung and pancreatic cancers.

The multi-centre, open-label trial focuses on individuals diagnosed with methylthioadenosine phosphorylase (MTAP)-deleted pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, alongside patients with MTAP-deleted and rat sarcoma virus (RAS)-mutant non-small cell lung cancer.

It is sponsored by Tango Therapeutics and consists of dose-escalation and expansion phases.

The dose-escalation phase primarily aims to identify the combination’s maximum tolerated dose.

Secondary measures include evaluating safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and antitumour activity.

Tango Therapeutics president and CEO Malte Peters said: “The encouraging clinical activity, durability and tolerability observed to date with vopimetostat in combination with RAS inhibition reinforce our belief that co-targeting PRMT5 and RAS represents a promising new frontier in the treatment of pancreatic cancer and potentially other RAS-driven cancers.

“We are thrilled to initiate this study in partnership with Erasca, a company leading the advancement of RAS-targeted therapies, to evaluate vopimetostat with ERAS-0015 and further explore the potential of this clinically validated and synergistic combination approach.”

Both investigational therapies target cancer pathways through distinct mechanisms.

ERAS-0015 is an oral pan-RAS molecular glue created to block RAS signalling and counter resistance to mutant-selective inhibitors by suppressing RAS wild-type variants.

Erasca is currently assessing the therapy in the AURORAS-1 Phase I trial for patients presenting with RAS-mutant solid tumours.

Initial dose escalation demonstrated linear pharmacokinetics alongside confirmed and unconfirmed partial responses at doses starting at 8mg once daily.

Vopimetostat is a once-daily oral protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) inhibitor evaluated by Tango Therapeutics as both a monotherapy and in combination.

In clinical evaluations to date, the therapy showed durable activity and a favourable tolerability profile across several MTAP-deleted cancers, including pancreatic and lung malignancies.

data.title: Merck begins Phase III ENHANCE-3 trial of Ohtuvayre in COPD
data.description:
Merck & Co (MSD) has begun the Phase III ENHANCE-3 clinical trial assessing Ohtuvayre (ensifentrine) to prevent exacerbations in adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

Patient recruitment has begun, with the initial participants enrolling in the US.

The placebo-controlled, randomised, double-blind study plans to enrol around 2,136 patients across 28 countries.

Eligible participants are adults aged 40 to 80 years with a verified COPD diagnosis for at least 12 months, a current or previous smoking history, and a documented moderate or severe exacerbation within the prior year while receiving standard care.

Individuals must have received consistent background therapy for at least two months. Subjects will be randomised 1:1 to twice-daily Ohtuvayre or placebo alongside their existing standard-of-care regimen.

The primary endpoint assesses the annualised rate of adjudicated moderate or severe exacerbations over 52 weeks.

Secondary measures examine overall safety and adjudicated severe exacerbations over 52 weeks, and quality of life through the St George’s Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) at week 24.

Permitted standard treatments include inhaled corticosteroids, long-acting beta-agonists, and long-acting muscarinic antagonists, or bronchodilators alone if corticosteroids are inappropriate.

MSD Research Laboratories global clinical development vice-president Dr Mahesh Patel said: “Many patients with COPD continue to experience persistent symptoms such as shortness of breath, despite current standard-of-care therapy. For these patients, exacerbations remain a major driver of disease progression and diminished quality of life.

“The initiation of the Phase III ENHANCE-3 study marks an important step in our efforts to further strengthen the body of evidence supporting Ohtuvayre and its potential to address significant unmet needs in COPD care. We remain committed to advancing innovative research to help the millions of people impacted by this disease worldwide.”

The US Food and Drug Administration approved Ohtuvayre in June 2024 for adult COPD maintenance based on data from the ENHANCE-1 and ENHANCE-2 studies.

Last month, MSD reported that the Phase IIb MK-7240-012 study of its investigational humanised monoclonal antibody, tulisokibart, achieved its primary endpoint for patients with moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa.

data.title: First patient dosed in Enanta’s Phase IIb/III trial for RSV
data.description:
Enanta Pharmaceuticals has dosed the first patient in its global Phase IIb/III RESOLVE trial assessing zelicapavir in high-risk adult outpatients diagnosed with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection.

Initial results from the Phase IIb segment of the programme are anticipated in 2027.

The double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, multi-centre study is assessing the safety and efficacy of zelicapavir in adults presenting with respiratory symptoms lasting no more than three days and a confirmed RSV diagnosis.

Enrolled participants must be at least 75 years old, have chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or suffer from congestive heart failure.

During the trial, subjects take an oral dose of 800mg of zelicapavir or a matched placebo once daily for seven days, followed by a 28-day assessment period.

The trial uses the duration until all 13 RSV symptoms fully resolve, measured using the RiiQ tool, as its primary endpoint.

Hospitalisation frequency serves as a key secondary measure, alongside overall safety, antiviral activity, and additional clinical efficacy outcomes.

At least 200 participants will take part in the Phase IIb portion to verify treatment effect sizes, while the Phase III stage is expected to enrol nearly 660 individuals.

Enanta Pharmaceuticals chief medical officer Scott Rottinghaus said: “We are excited to advance our zelicapavir programme into a Phase IIb/III study with the dosing of the first patient in RESOLVE. Based on learnings from our Phase II RSVHR study, the RESOLVE trial is enrolling adults at high risk for severe outcomes from RSV.

“The Phase IIb portion is designed to confirm the treatment effect size and generate an additional dataset with the goal of strengthening the clinical evidence supporting zelicapavir.

“Together with LOTUS, our paediatric Phase IIb trial, this progress positions us to deliver two important Phase IIb data readouts in 2027 and marks a significant step forward in the development of zelicapavir.”

Zelicapavir holds fast track designation from the US Food and Drug Administration. Unlike RSV fusion inhibitors that prevent viral entry, the compound inhibits the RSV N-protein to halt viral replication across RSV-A and RSV-B strains.

In earlier Phase II testing involving high-risk adults, the therapy shortened the time needed to resolve all 13 symptoms by 6.7 days compared to placebo in patients matching the RESOLVE criteria.

That earlier study also recorded an RSV-related hospitalisation rate of 0% in treated patients compared to 5% in the placebo cohort.

In a paediatric Phase II trial of children aged 28 days to three years, the therapy also demonstrated antiviral activity and accelerated symptom resolution. Across clinical trials, zelicapavir has been administered to more than 700 individuals.

Enanta Pharmaceuticals focuses on discovering small molecule treatments for immunological diseases and viral infections.

data.title: Pfizer reports Phase II data for 25vPnC infant vaccine candidate
data.description:
Pfizer has reported findings from a Phase II trial assessing PF-07872412 (25vPnC), its investigational 25-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine candidate, in infants.

The results showed that a four-dose regimen provoked immune responses against all 25 assessed serotypes.

Safety and tolerability profiles were comparable to four doses of Pneumococcal 20-valent Conjugate Vaccine (PREVNAR 20).

According to findings, immune responses occurred across every evaluated serotype one month following the third and fourth doses.

These included five additional serotypes, 15A, 23A, 23B, 24F, and 35B, estimated to cause a further 30% of paediatric invasive pneumococcal disease cases in the US compared with PREVNAR 20.

The candidate specifically targets serotype 3, responsible for 10.6% of invasive cases in US children aged under five years.

Compared with PREVNAR 20, geometric mean concentrations for serotype 3 were 8.8 times higher one month after the third dose and 15 times higher one month after the fourth dose.

Assays measuring opsonophagocytic activity also showed booster effects across all 25 serotypes one month after the fourth dose.

Adverse events, systemic occurrences, and local reactions remained balanced between the 25vPnC and PREVNAR 20 cohorts, reflecting medical conditions typical for healthy infants. Investigators recorded no related serious adverse events.

Pfizer senior vice-president and chief vaccines officer Annaliesa Anderson said: “These encouraging data build on more than 25 years of progress in protecting children from serious pneumococcal disease with PREVNAR vaccines.

“By expanding serotype coverage and applying next-generation technology to the historically challenging serotype 3, this candidate aims to extend the substantial reductions in disease that existing vaccines have achieved.

“If successful, it could help provide children with the broadest protection against invasive pneumococcal disease to date.”

The findings support Pfizer’s paediatric Phase III programme. Launched earlier in 2026, the programme includes three trials evaluating up to 6,830 children randomised to receive either 25vPnC or PREVNAR 20.

The serotypes in 25vPnC represent around 84% of invasive pneumococcal disease cases among US children younger than five years old.

Pfizer has also completed participant enrolment in an additional Phase III trial assessing manufacturing consistency across three separate lots of 25vPnC.

Separately, the company aims to advance an adult fifth-generation, 35-valent vaccine candidate into clinical studies before the close of 2026, subject to regulatory alignment.

In June, Pfizer reported topline data from the Phase III SigVie-002 study investigating sigvotatug vedotin in adults with previously treated, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
